seo_title: Cost of Living in Lisbon 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Lisbon per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A warm, friendly Atlantic city with D7 and Digital Nomad visas. The most open part of Europe for remote workers, but with rising rental prices.
pros: Digital Nomad Visa and D7 for remote workers and passive income
A mild Atlantic climate — a warm winter at +15°C
English is widespread in Lisbon and Porto
The NHR tax break (though it's being wound down)
cons: Rent has doubled in five years
Distance from the EU centre and expensive flights
NHR was reformed in 2024 — fewer tax advantages
A competitive job market for local positions

visa_steps.title: Digital Nomad Visa
visa_steps.description: For remote workers with income from €3,280/month — issued at the embassy.

visa_steps.title: D7 Visa
visa_steps.description: For the financially independent with passive income — pension, rent, dividends.

visa_steps.description: Obtained remotely through a lawyer or in person — needed for everything.

faq.question: Which visa suits a remote worker in Lisbon?
faq.answer: The Digital Nomad Visa — issued for income from €3,280/month. The D7 is for passive income.

faq.question: What about NHR in Lisbon?
faq.answer: From 2024 the benefits were cut. For those arriving in 2024+ it's IFICI, with a 20% tax on professional income for 5 years.

faq.question: Is English enough day to day in Lisbon?
faq.answer: In Lisbon and Porto — yes. In the regions Portuguese is essential.

faq.question: How much is rent in Lisbon?
faq.answer: A one-bedroom in the centre runs 100,000–160,000 ₽, the outskirts 60,000–95,000 ₽. It depends heavily on the district.

faq.question: How is banking for Russians in Lisbon?
faq.answer: Activobank is the most accommodating and opens accounts remotely. Millennium — after VR processing.

faq.question: Where should I live in Lisbon?
faq.answer: Príncipe Real and Campo de Ourique are trendy. Alvalade is for families. Almada is cheaper, across the bridge.

reviews.text: Got the DNV in 4 months. Lisbon means calm, the ocean and English. The downside — rent has risen and NHR is shrinking.
The best climate in Europe, safety like Scandinavia. The bureaucracy runs at a Portuguese pace — you have to get used to it.
